records.public_safe_text: on may 8, 2025, i, officer o. mckinney, was assigned to velasquez elementary as the campus police officer. at approximately 7:25 a. m., i was notified of an auto-ped accident in the parking lot of the [roadway] at approximately 7:11 a. m., and the driver of the vehicle had already left the scene. however, i spoke with tykenya spann (teacher/pedestrian), and she informed me that the driver had hit her left leg with the fr part of his vehicle while she was directing [school facility]. during my investigation, i reviewed surveillance cameras at velasquez elementary. at approximately 7:11 a. m., i observed the driver, now identified as paulo morales, enter the crosswalk as tykenya directed the traffic to stop. however, i observed [roadway] into the crosswalk, causing a near collision with tykenya. tykena placed both of her hands on the fr side of paulo's hood, and before making full contact with tykenya, paulo came to a stop, which prevented him from colliding with tykenya. during further investigation, paulo reported that his front windshield was hazy, which limited his visibility. paulo also stated that the sun was beaming on his window, and that caused his visibility to be limited as well. upon completion of the investigation, it appeared that paulo did not strike the left side of tykenya's leg as was reported.

(head trauma, and femur injury). a patrol crash investigator arrived on scene (see supplement)mia statement: mia was not injured but scared, mia was travelling westbound on martin luther king jr, [roadway] northbound. mia made a left turn as the light was green to turn left on martin luther king jr. the light at the consecutive intersection of martin [roadway] southbound was green, going 35-45mpoh, mia then observed a male upon impact of the male and vehicle colliding. the male was riding the scooter facing southbound, after the scooter struck the vehicle, the male flew and made contact with the kia. smith statement: nick was stationary at a red light facing eastbound on martin luther king jr, nick observed the male that was struck as he ran from south curbline to north curbline to grab a scooter, nick assumed as the male was running across that he was not permitted to cross as of yet. nick observed the male [roadway], as he was crossing that is when mia (mini cooper) made contact with the male. the male then struck smith's stationary vehicle. witness statement: mercedes only observed the collision and no other evidentiary information besides the collision

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was [roadway]. unit 3 was parked in the roadway facing sb. the occupants of unit 3 were attempting to get an intoxicated pedestrian (unit 2) into unit 3. the pedestrian refused to comply with the occupants of unit 3. the driver of unit 1 passed unit 3 on the left side of the roadway. it is unclear if the pedestrian was standing or had fallen, but he was run over by unit 1 and died as a result. the occupants for unit 3 were the driver sitting in the front left seat and the passenger was getting into unit 3 when the pedestrian was struck. there was no damage or transfer from the pedestrian to unit 1. the pedestrian was taken for an autopsy and toxicology. the driver of unit 1 consented to the pbt with low results and did not show any signs of intoxication on the hgn test. he also provided a voluntary blood specimen. the driver of unit 3 showed no signs of intoxication. ***[date] supplement*** toxicology shows the driver of unit 1 was not intoxicated. the pedestrian (unit 2) showed to have a bac of 0. 232.
